title: DMSO-free cryopreservation of hiPSC-derived cardiomyocytes: low temperature characterization and protocol development.
study_design: DMSO-free CPA optimization using trehalose, glycerol, and isoleucine, followed by controlled-rate freezing, nucleation-temperature optimization, osmotic characterization, and post-thaw cardiac-function testing.
interventions: DMSO-free trehalose/glycerol/isoleucine CPA in Normosol R

experiments.model: Cardiomyocytes from one engineered human CCND2 hiPSC line
experiments.intervention: DMSO-free CPA composed of trehalose, glycerol, and isoleucine in Normosol R
experiments.cooling: Optimizer evaluated at 1 °C/min and nucleation at −4 °C; later thermal optimization is a separate stage
experiments.storage: Liquid-nitrogen vapor storage; duration not reported in the inspected methods
experiments.result: Differential evolution used nine population entries per generation, with eight archived populations (0–7) and convergence after generation 6. Three selected formulations exceeded 90% recovery; optimizer-stage DMSO controls averaged 69.4 ± 6.4%. Figure 2 composition levels are arbitrary units, not absolute concentrations.
experiments.sample_size: 72 population entries across eight generations; retained solutions can recur and entries are not independent donors
experiments.source_locator: Results, DE algorithm-driven DMSO-free CPA optimization; Fig. 2

experiments.model: Cardiomyocytes from one engineered human CCND2 hiPSC line
experiments.storage: Liquid-nitrogen vapor storage; duration not reported in the inspected methods
experiments.timepoint: Immediate post-thaw count before wash; live post-thaw / live pre-freeze
experiments.result: Selected thermal settings were 5 °C/min cooling and −8 °C nucleation. Original tables contain 24 cooling-rate and 24 nucleation-temperature observations, four per arm/setting. These compare Solution A with 10% DMSO; batch identity is absent from the workbook.
experiments.sample_size: n=4 per condition and CPA in Fig. 3; three batches for nucleation optimization
experiments.source_locator: Results, Cooling rate optimization and Nucleation Temperature Optimization; Fig. 3

experiments.model: Cardiomyocytes from one engineered human CCND2 hiPSC line
experiments.comparator: 10% DMSO and freshly replated unfrozen cells
experiments.storage: Liquid-nitrogen vapor storage; duration not reported in the inspected methods
experiments.outcome_name: Post-thaw recovery, cardiac markers, and calcium transients
experiments.timepoint: post-thaw culture for 1 week; calcium transient assay after replating/monolayer formation
experiments.result: Original final-validation rows reproduce Solution A 92.0625%, Solution B 89.875%, and DMSO 80.1875% recovery (four observations each); A minus DMSO is 11.875 percentage points. The paper's ±2.50 and ±4.22 values match population SD; sample SEMs are 1.4447 and 2.4375 percentage points. Solution B had reduced calcium signal despite high recovery. The reported lack of a significant signal difference for A/DMSO versus fresh cells is not an equivalence result, and the amplitude normalization is unresolved.
experiments.sample_size: Recovery n=4 observations per arm; calcium n=7 fresh, n=5 A, n=3 B and DMSO; one donor line
experiments.source_locator: Results, Post-thaw functional assessment; Figures 6–7; original supplement Post-thaw assessment (recovery) rows 2–13 and (calcium) rows 2–19
experiments.evidence_excerpt: calcium signal amplitude of the DMSO-free Solution A

main_finding: In one engineered CCND2 hiPSC-cardiomyocyte line, optimized DMSO-free Solution A yielded 92.06% live-cell recovery versus 80.19% for the optimized DMSO comparator; Solution B illustrates that high recovery can coexist with impaired calcium signaling.
limitations: Figure 2 uses dimensionless composition levels; no mapping to absolute trehalose/glycerol/isoleucine concentrations was found in the inspected article or original supplement. A reproducible formulation cannot be inferred.
Recovery is explicitly live cells after thaw divided by live cells before freezing (Equation 1), not post-thaw live fraction. Supplementary tables do not provide underlying cell counts.
One engineered CCND2 donor line; four recovery observations per final arm are not four donors. Batch/trace identifiers and cross-panel independence are unresolved.
DMSO-free loading was 60 minutes versus 30 minutes for DMSO; loading and composition effects are confounded.
Final recovery prose ± values reproduce population SD, although the general figure legend describes SEM. Do not report those ± values as SEM.
All 18 stored calcium amplitudes equal peak minus minimum, whereas the paper labels the endpoint F/F0. Upstream normalization is not documented in the inspected tables.
Calcium was measured after monolayer formation; its exact day is not reported. Nonsignificant differences from fresh cells do not establish equivalence.
Optimizer-stage DMSO recovery of 69.4% is a different comparator stage from final-validation recovery of 80.19%.
mechanism_claim: The study directly measured CPA recovery, low-temperature behavior, osmotic response, markers, and calcium transients. Osmolyte-mediated protection and osmotic management are interpretations supported by these measurements, not proof of a single molecular mechanism.
reviewer: Luna extraction; root methods/results, Figure 2/6 visual review and original-supplement recomputation
